name: Cohere API token pricing (serverless, per 1M tokens, 2026-10-04 list price)
region: Cohere cloud (North America / EU endpoints; not separately priced)
price_basis: USD per 1M TOKENS, LIST PRICE, observed 2026-10-04. Command family: Command-light $0.30 input / $0.60 output; Command R 03-2024 $0.50 / $1.50; Command (current) $1.00 / $2.00; Command R+ 04-2024 $3.00 / $15.00; Command R+ 08-2024 $2.50 / $10.00. Aya Expanse 8B and 32B on the API $0.50 input / $1.50 output. price_usd = Command-light input. The page also carries seat pricing ($3.00/$5.00-class figures at $2,000-$6,500 tiers) which are CONSOLE subscriptions, not API rates - do not mix them.
notes: Cohere is the outlier here in that its headline chat model is not the cheapest thing it sells: the OLDER Command-light at $0.30/$0.60 is less than half the price of current Command at $1.00/$2.00. Anyone reading 'Cohere costs $1/$2' as the family rate is quoting the wrong row for anyone optimizing cost. Second observation: the versioned R+ snapshots span $2.50-$3.00 in and $10-$15 out on the SAME nominal model name, i.e. a version bump can move price by 40% in either direction, so pin the exact model version in any cost model. Cohere's billing floor matters too: API calls from a Trial key are free, production keys bill at end of calendar month or once $250 is outstanding. No GPU hourly rate published - Cohere's serving hardware is not a product.
